title: The Brauer group of a smooth curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve over
algebraically closed $k$. Then its Brauer group ([def-br]) vanishes:

$$
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0.
$$

proof.text: By [lem-sc-compactification] and [lem-sc-affine-open-proper], a smooth separated connected curve is either proper or affine, and we treat the two cases.

*Proper case.* Let $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(C)\to C$ be the generic point. By [lem-sc-brauer-injectivity],

$$
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Br}(k(C)),
$$
and the target is zero by [lem-sc-tsen].

*Affine case.* Let $\overline C$ be the compactification of [lem-sc-compactification] and $S:=\overline C\setminus C\neq\emptyset$ the finite complement ([lem-sc-dim0-finite]; nonempty because a proper affine curve is finite, [lem-sc-proper-affine-finite]). The divisor exact sequence ([lem-sc-divisor-exact-sequence])

$$
0\to\mathbf G_m\to j_*\mathbf G_m\to\bigoplus_{P\in S}i_{P*}\mathbf Z\to0
$$

on $\overline C_{\Et}$ gives, using [lem-sc-open-curve-gm-direct-image-cohomology] to identify $H^q(\overline C_{\Et},j_*\mathbf G_m)$ with $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)$ for $q\leq2$, the exact sequence

$$
H^2(\overline C,\mathbf G_m)\to H^2(C,\mathbf G_m)\to H^2(\overline C,\textstyle\bigoplus_{P\in S}i_{P*}\mathbf Z).
$$

 For each $P$, the closed immersion $i_P$ is finite, so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exactness of $i_{P*}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] identifies $H^q(\overline C,i_{P*}\mathbf Z)$ with $H^q(\operatorname{Spec}k(P),\mathbf Z)$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, $k(P)=k$, so [lem-sc-point-z-cohomology] makes this zero for $q\geq1$. Cohomology commutes with the finite direct sum over $P\in S$. The proper case gives $H^2(\overline C,\mathbf G_m)=0$, hence $H^2(C,\mathbf G_m)=0$.
